==Problem==

Six trees are equally spaced along one side of a straight road. The distance from the first tree to the fourth is 60 feet. What is the distance in feet between the first and last trees?

<math>\text{(A)}\ 90 \qquad \text{(B)}\ 100 \qquad \text{(C)}\ 105 \qquad \text{(D)}\ 120 \qquad \text{(E)}\ 140</math>

==Solution==

There are <math> 3 </math> spaces between the 1st and 4th trees, so each of these spaces has <math> \frac{60}{3}=20 </math> feet. Between the first and last trees there are <math> 5 </math> spaces, so the distance between them is <math> 20\times5=100 </math> feet, <math> \boxed{\text{B}} </math>.
